summaries.summary: Production runs on Modal via `backend/modal_app.py`, deployed by hand (`modal deploy modal_app.py`); there is no CI deploy job. Three images are built (api_image = python deps only; latex_image = python deps + texlive + poppler; worker_image = python deps only), all with `DEPLOY_TARGET=modal` baked in and all secrets coming from the single Modal secret `latexy-backend-secrets`. The FastAPI app is served by `@modal.asgi_app()` on api_image; eight `@app.function` entrypoints wrap Celery tasks and run them synchronously with `task.apply(kwargs=payload, throw=False)`, so Celery's broker/result backend and its retry machinery are bypassed entirely. Dispatch from the API goes through `app/core/modal_dispatch.spawn()`, which is only reached from nine hand-written `if os.environ.get("DEPLOY_TARGET") == "modal"` branches in latex_worker, llm_worker, orchestrator, ats_worker (x4) and cleanup_worker (x2). Everything else that enqueues work — cover letters, interview prep, document conversion, auto-save checkpoints, completion/digest email — has no Modal branch and no Modal function, so it still calls `apply_async` against `CELERY_BROKER_URL` with no consumer anywhere. There is no Celery beat and no `modal.Period`/`schedule=` anywhere in modal_app.py, so every periodic task is dead in production. `grep -rn "DEPLOY_TARGET\|modal" backend/test` returns zero hits: every one of these divergences is exercised only on the local Celery side, and the Modal side has never been executed by a test. That is the same blind spot that produced both P0s (#954, #956), and the findings below are the remaining members of that class.

The compile path has three engine invocation styles: a Docker-sandboxed `docker run` (used whenever `shutil.which("docker")` is truthy), an in-process engine gated by `local_engine_allowed()`, and a set of post-hoc read-confinement checks. Hardening flags (`-no-shell-escape`, `-recorder`, `openin_any=p`, `openout_any=p`, `shell_escape=f`, `max_print_line=10000`) are applied to every invocation via `LATEX_SANDBOX_FLAGS`/`engine_env()`. Reads are policed twice: `find_engine_read_escape()` scans each transcript line for `(<path>` tokens and kills the process before the file's bytes are streamed, and `find_recorder_read_escape()` parses the `-recorder` `.fls` after the run (fail-closed on a missing or NUL-padded/self-referential recorder file) before any PDF/log/text is published. Hotfix acdf4316 did two things: it added `DEPLOY_TARGET == "modal"` to `local_engine_allowed()` (gVisor cgroups carry no docker/kubepods marker), and it switched the two worker call sites to a relative main filename plus `-output-directory .` with `cwd=job_dir`, because `openin_any=p` rejects absolute read paths. (a) I simulated all five topologies by monkeypatching `/.dockerenv`, `KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST`, `/proc/self/cgroup`, `ENVIRONMENT` and `DEPLOY_TARGET`: modal→True, docker→True, k8s→True, bare-host-prod→False (intended), bare-host-dev→True. The gate is now correct for every real topology — except that any non-truthy `ALLOW_LOCAL_LATEX_ENGINE` (including `""`) still overrides all of it (finding 4). (b) No call site passes an absolute *input* path any more; the two remaining sites in latex_service.py still pass an absolute `-output-directory`, which is the TeX Live default-safe combination, but they were left inconsistent with the hotfix (finding 5). (c) All 56 shipped templates in `backend/app/data/templates` pass `validate_latex_content()`; there is no asset-upload/multi-file support in the compile path at all, so `\includegraphics`/`\input` of user files is not a real code path today. (d) The confinement layers are unchanged by the hotfix and I verified them empirically on the pure functions: `\input{/etc/passwd}`, `\makeatletter\@@input`, `\csname input\endcsname{}`, `\lstinputlisting{/abs}`, literal `\openin`, `..` traversal and `\write 18{}` are all rejected pre-compile; the two documented walk-throughs (`\newcommand{\zz}{\input}\zz{/etc/passwd}` and `\csname openi\string n\endcsname`) still pass the validator but are caught by the transcript layer and the recorder layer respectively, and are additionally blocked outright by `openin_any=p` in production. I found no weakening of read confinement from the relative-path change. The real remaining risk is elsewhere: the Modal API container has no TeX at all, and Modal has no scheduler.

PR #951 (merge fac3be1b) landed four cross-cutting subsystems on top of 59b2fca8: (1) a numeric usage-quota meter (`config.PLAN_QUOTAS` + `EntitlementService.consume_quota/enforce_quota`) wired into every compile/optimize/AI-assist route, counting in Redis DB 1 via `get_redis_cache_client()`; (2) a LaTeX sandbox in `latex_service.py` that runs the engine with `openin_any/openout_any=p`, `-recorder`, a stripped env, and then post-validates the kpathsea `.fls` recorder file against an allowlist of TeX-tree roots, failing the whole job if the engine touched anything else; (3) a MinIO orphan pruner in `cleanup_worker.py` guarded by a Redis "which database indexed these objects" stamp in `workers/storage_guard.py`; (4) a proxy-aware rate-limit bucket helper `client_ip_id()` now shared by the global middleware and every per-route limiter. `main.py` middleware ordering is correct and did NOT undo #948/#950 — I verified a live 429 still carries `access-control-allow-origin`, `retry-after` and `access-control-expose-headers`, and the single-EVAL Lua limiter from #950 is intact. The analytics `group_by` rewrite is also fine (`/analytics/me` returns 200 with daily_activity). The real risk is concentrated in the sandbox's recorder allowlist and in the quota meter's new hard dependency on `REDIS_CACHE_URL`, both of which behave differently on Modal (no docker engine, no nginx, no celery beat) than they do locally.

PR #951 (fac3be1b) added a numeric usage meter on top of the pre-existing boolean entitlement engine. `config.PLAN_QUOTAS` is the single enforced source of truth (free: 10 compilations/day, 3 optimizations/month, 25 ai_assists/month; basic: 50/10/100 monthly; pro/byok/team unlimited), and `_sync_plan_feature_copy()` rewrites the marketing strings in `SUBSCRIPTION_PLANS[...]["features"]` from that table at import time so `/subscription/plans` cannot drift from enforcement — I verified the served copy matches (`free: {"compilations": "10 / day", "optimizations": "3 / month"}`). Counters live in the CACHE Redis (`REDIS_CACHE_URL`, db 1) at `latexy:quota:{dimension}:{user_id}:{period}` and are bumped with a single INCRBY, so the counter is genuinely atomic: I fired 20 parallel `/jobs/submit` compiles against the free 10/day limit twice and got exactly 10x200 / 10x402 both times, with the counter landing on exactly 10. Denied requests roll their increment back with DECRBY, and the period is embedded in the key so day/month rollover is implicit and needs no cron; refunds use the ticket's stored period, so a refund that crosses midnight still targets the window it charged. Routes that were wired up correctly: `/jobs/submit` (compile/optimize/combined), `/jobs/compile-watermarked`, `/jobs/batch`, `/compile`, `/optimize`, `/resumes/{id}/quick-tailor`, `/resumes/{id}/academic-cv-convert`, `/formats/upload`, and every platform-key LLM endpoint in `ai_routes.py` — all verified 402ing once the counter is at the limit. The failure policy is deliberately fail-CLOSED, which is the same class of guard that caused the two P0 outages, and it now hangs off an env var (`REDIS_CACHE_URL`) that is not validated in production and is not mentioned anywhere in the Modal deployment. Three real money-spending routes were missed by the sweep entirely, and the developer-API-key path bypasses the plan meter completely.

Latexy has two independent WebSocket surfaces. `/ws/jobs` is a singleton browser socket (frontend/src/lib/ws-client.ts) that multiplexes every job on the page: it forwards the Better Auth token as `?token=`, re-opens itself when the token changes mid-CONNECTING, re-subscribes all jobs on reconnect with a per-job Redis-Stream watermark, and drops non-monotonic stream IDs so the non-idempotent reducer never double-applies a replay. Backend `jobs_websocket` authorises each subscribe/cancel against `latexy:job:{id}:meta`, replays from the stream via EventBusManager, rate-limits to 20 msg/s, and sends a `sys.heartbeat` every 30 s. `/ws/collab/{resume_id}` is a hand-written Y.js/lib0 relay: it authenticates the session, resolves owner/collaborator role, relays SYNC/AWARENESS frames to peers (locally and cross-worker over Redis Pub/Sub), rejects document writes from viewer/commenter roles with a custom MSG_PERMISSION_DENIED (63) frame, and can terminate a user's live sockets on revocation. The merge of PR #951 kept both REST fallbacks that were meant to cover a Pub/Sub fanout failure: useJobStream has its own 4 s `getJobState` loop (from #931/#933) and useJobStatus layers a second 5 s loop on top, whose activity predicate #951 widened to include `idle`. I verified empirically against the live stack that exactly one live `/ws/jobs` socket survives, subscribe/replay works, events are delivered in order with no duplicated log lines, and collab role enforcement plus revocation behave correctly. Two real defects showed up: a promoted collaborator is told their access was revoked and permanently locked read-only, and every solo editor's collab socket is force-reconnected every 30 s.

Latexy's backend is a FastAPI app whose real production deployment is Modal (backend/modal_app.py), where DEPLOY_TARGET=modal switches worker dispatch from Celery to modal_dispatch.spawn(). Locally the same code runs the Celery path. PR #951 (fac3be1b) introduced a Redis-backed plan-quota meter (entitlement_service.consume_quota, PLAN_QUOTAS) and wired it into backend/app/api/job_routes.py, plus worker-side artifact persistence and Compilation-row reconciliation. Two P0 hotfixes (67efab7b, acdf4316) already had to undo fail-closed guards that took prod down. This audit covered the lx_sk_ developer API, the ATS worker's asyncio.run pattern, export_routes and the 12 parsers, trial_service, boot-time work in main.py, and — critically — the Modal-only branches, which had never been audited. The dominant theme found is production/local divergence: the Modal images and secret list do not carry things that exist locally (texlive in the API image, tesseract/poppler, REDIS_CACHE_URL, MinIO), and several Celery submit helpers have no Modal branch at all, so whole features silently never execute in production. The single most concrete regression is that the new quota meter has an unpatched parallel entrypoint: the developer API. All findings below were verified against the running stack or by direct execution.

confirmed.title: Nothing schedules periodic tasks on Modal — the MinIO orphan pruner, storage_guard stamp, temp-file cleanup, expired-job cleanup, health check and weekly digest never run in production
confirmed.introducedBy: pruner + storage_guard: fac3be1b (PR #951); absence of a Modal scheduler: pre-existing
confirmed.evidence: celery_app.py:103 defines beat_schedule with cleanup-expired-jobs (3600s), cleanup-temp-files (1800s), health-check (300s), weekly-digest-monday-9am and sample-queue-depths (20s). Celery beat is only launched by scripts/dev.sh and the docker/k8s manifests. `grep -n "schedule\|Period\|cron" backend/modal_app.py` → nothing; the file defines only `@app.function(... min_containers/scaledown_window ...)` entrypoints invoked by `.spawn()`. The only caller of the pruner is `cleanup_expired_jobs_task` (cleanup_worker.py:419 `minio_prune = _prune_orphaned_compilation_objects()`), which on Modal is reachable ONLY from the manual admin endpoint job_routes.py:1131.
confirmed.impact: The unbounded-storage-growth vector under `compilations/` that PR #951 was written to close is still open in production, and so is Redis job-state growth from expired jobs and /tmp growth in the warm min_containers=1 latex container (which now lives for hours, unlike a per-job container). The storage_guard DB-identity stamp is written on every Modal compile but never read, so all of storage_guard.py is dead code in production. The health-check task and queue-depth metrics also never fire, so the observability added alongside is blind.
confirmed.repro: Read backend/modal_app.py end to end: there is no scheduled function. Any beat_schedule entry therefore has no execution path under DEPLOY_TARGET=modal.
confirmed.fix: Add scheduled Modal functions, e.g. `@app.function(image=worker_image, secrets=_secrets, schedule=modal.Period(hours=1))` calling `cleanup_expired_jobs_task.apply(throw=False)` and `modal.Period(minutes=30)` for `cleanup_temp_files_task`, plus a weekly `modal.Cron("0 9 * * 1")` for the digest. Until then, treat the pruner/storage_guard part of #951 as unshipped.
confirmed.correction:
Corrected claim: There is no scheduler in the Modal deployment — backend/modal_app.py defines only spawn-invoked worker entrypoints and the ASGI app, with no schedule=/modal.Period/modal.Cron anywhere in backend/. Every entry in celery_app.py:103's beat_schedule is therefore unreachable under DEPLOY_TARGET=modal, since Celery beat is only started by docker-compose/k8s/dev.sh.

The two consequences that actually bite in production are:
(a) compilations/ in object storage grows without bound. The orphan pruner added by fac3be1b (PR #951) is reachable only from the admin-gated POST /jobs/system/cleanup (job_routes.py:1131), and storage_service.py sets no bucket lifecycle policy. This is the exact vector #951 was written to close, and it remains open.
(b) The Monday 09:00 weekly digest (email_worker.send_weekly_digest_to_all) never fires when EMAIL_ENABLED is true.
A lesser third: stuck jobs are never proactively marked timed-out.

The other claimed impacts do not hold. Redis job state is not unbounded — event_publisher.py writes every job key with a 24h TTL (_DEFAULT_TTL=86400; setex at 158/176/197, expire at 80/127). /tmp does not accumulate — latex_worker.py:847-851 rmtree's job_dir in a finally on every path, and scaledown_window=120 keeps containers short-lived. The queue-depth sampler measures Celery broker LLEN, structurally always 0 on Modal (tasks run in-process via .apply()), so its absence loses nothing; health_check_task likewise only writes events nobody reads, while GET /health and GET /api/v1/jobs/health provide real health. storage_guard.py is only half dead: record_compilation_database runs on every Modal compile (latex_worker.py:342); only the read path is unused.

Attribution as stated is correct: the pruner and storage_guard are new in fac3be1b (PR #951); the missing Modal scheduler is pre-existing (modal_app.py never had one since f2b6ee09).

Severity: medium rather than high — one unbounded-growth vector in object storage plus a silently-dead email digest, not the six-way failure described.

confirmed.title: Five task submitters have no Modal branch and no corresponding Modal function: cover letters, interview prep, document conversion, auto-save checkpoints and all email
confirmed.introducedBy: pre-existing (Modal branches were added task-by-task); the ai_assists quota charge in format_routes is fac3be1b (PR #951)
confirmed.location: backend/app/workers/cover_letter_worker.py:360, backend/app/workers/converter_worker.py:196, backend/app/workers/interview_prep_worker.py:282, backend/app/workers/orchestrator.py:298 & :310, backend/app/workers/latex_worker.py:759, backend/app/workers/email_worker.py:247 — vs backend/modal_app.py (functions defined: run_latex_task, run_orchestrator_task, run_llm_task, run_ats_task, run_jd_analysis_task, run_deep_analyze_task, run_embed_resume_task, run_cleanup_task)
confirmed.evidence: `grep -rn "apply_async" backend/app` lists 17 sites; only 9 are preceded by an `if os.environ.get("DEPLOY_TARGET") == "modal"` branch. cover_letter_worker.py:360 `generate_cover_letter_task.apply_async(args=[resume_latex, job_description], ...)` has no such guard, and neither do converter_worker.py:196 or interview_prep_worker.py:282. celery_app.py:36 `broker=settings.CELERY_BROKER_URL`, whose default (config.py:263) is `redis://localhost:6379/0`. These endpoints are shipped: cover_letter_routes.py:316, interview_routes.py:125, format_routes.py:447.
confirmed.impact: On Modal, POST /cover-letters, the interview-prep generator and the document-conversion upload either (a) raise kombu OperationalError against localhost:6379 → 500, or (b) if CELERY_BROKER_URL is in the secret, succeed in publishing to a queue no worker consumes → the job never reaches a terminal state and the UI spins forever. For document conversion the new ai_assists quota is charged at format_routes.py:434 BEFORE the enqueue and only refunded if the enqueue raises, so in case (b) the user's allowance is silently burned for a job that will never run. Auto-save checkpoints after a compile (latex_worker.py:759, orchestrator.py:298) are wrapped in try/except and fail silently, so the post-optimization auto-save simply never happens in production.
confirmed.repro: Read the three submit_* functions; none contains the DEPLOY_TARGET check that the sibling submit_latex_compilation (latex_worker.py:880) has. Cross-check against the eight function names defined in modal_app.py.
confirmed.fix: Add `run_cover_letter_task`, `run_interview_prep_task`, `run_converter_task`, `run_auto_save_task` and `run_email_task` Modal functions and the matching DEPLOY_TARGET branches — or, better, replace the nine copy-pasted branches with one dispatch helper that maps task name → Modal function and raises loudly at import time if a submitter has no mapping, so the next feature cannot silently regress the same way.
confirmed.correction: Core defect confirmed and high severity, but scope it to the three user-facing paths. On DEPLOY_TARGET=modal, submit_cover_letter_generation (cover_letter_worker.py:360), submit_interview_prep_generation (interview_prep_worker.py:282) and submit_document_conversion (converter_worker.py:196) call Celery apply_async with no Modal dispatch branch and no corresponding Modal function, so POST /cover-letters, the interview-prep generator and the document-conversion upload can never complete in production. Post-compile auto-save checkpoints (latex_worker.py:759, orchestrator.py:298) are a real but silent lower-severity loss. The email items (orchestrator.py:310, email_worker.py:247) should be dropped from this finding: send_weekly_digest is only invoked from celery beat, which is not deployed on Modal at all, and job-completion email is gated on EMAIL_ENABLED — email is absent on Modal independently of these call sites. The ai_assists quota burn (fac3be1b) is conditional: it only occurs if CELERY_BROKER_URL is set to a reachable broker in the Modal secret; if it defaults to localhost the enqueue raises and the existing refund path at format_routes.py:458 works correctly.

confirmed.title: api_image has no LaTeX toolchain, but three shipped routes compile pdflatex in-process inside the API container
confirmed.introducedBy: pre-existing image split; made silent by acdf4316 (PR #956), which now lets local_engine_allowed() return True on Modal before checking whether an engine exists
confirmed.location: backend/modal_app.py:43-49 (api_image installs only gcc/g++/libpq-dev/curl), backend/app/api/routes.py:357 POST /compile → :403, routes.py:637 POST /optimize-and-compile → :664, routes.py:781 POST /public/compile → :839; backend/app/services/latex_service.py:456-485
confirmed.evidence: api_image: `.apt_install(*_APT_BASE)` where `_APT_BASE = ["gcc", "g++", "libpq-dev", "curl"]` — no texlive, no latexmk, no docker CLI. latex_service.compile_latex falls to the local branch (`docker_engine_available()` is `shutil.which("docker") is not None`, false in api_image), then `assert_local_engine_allowed(job_id)` now passes because local_engine_allowed() short-circuits on `(settings.DEPLOY_TARGET or "").lower() == "modal"`, and then execs `["pdflatex", ...]` which does not exist. Verified the endpoint is live and works locally only because the dev box HAS docker: `curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8030/compile -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" -F file=@/tmp/aud.tex` → `{"success":true,"job_id":"ffcf5b6a-...","compilation_time":1.46,"pdf_size":13164}`. `which docker` → /usr/local/bin/docker; `which pdflatex` → not found.
confirmed.impact: POST /compile (the endpoint the TUI's `/compile <file>` uses — packages/tui/src/tools/compile.ts:52 `client.postForm('/compile', form)`), POST /public/compile (anonymous trial compile) and POST /optimize-and-compile all fail with FileNotFoundError → 500 in production. The quota is refunded on the exception path so users are not double-charged, but the features are simply broken. The /health endpoint hides this: routes.py:262 `latex_available = True if os.environ.get("DEPLOY_TARGET") == "modal" else latex_compiler.is_available()` reports LaTeX as available unconditionally on Modal even in the API container that has no engine.
confirmed.repro: Locally the docker branch is taken, so this cannot reproduce on the dev box — that is the point. Inspect api_image's apt list and follow latex_service.compile_latex's else branch.
confirmed.fix: Either route these three endpoints through `spawn("run_latex_task", ...)` like /jobs/submit does, or build the API on latex_image. Additionally, make `local_engine_allowed()` also verify `shutil.which(compiler)` so a container without an engine reports ENGINE_UNAVAILABLE (a clean 503) instead of an opaque 500.
confirmed.correction:
Corrected claim (severity: medium, not high):

1. IMPACT IS WRONG — it is not a 500 and the quota is NOT refunded. compile_latex wraps the whole body in `except Exception` (latex_service.py:572-578) and returns CompilationResponse(success=False, message="Compilation error: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'pdflatex'"). Verified by direct execution. Because no exception reaches the route handler, POST /compile returns HTTP 200 with success=false AND the `except Exception: refund_quota` branch never runs — the user's monthly compilation allowance is silently consumed for a compile that never happened, and the raw errno string is echoed to the client. That is the opposite of the finding's "quota is refunded on the exception path so users are not double-charged".

2. ATTRIBUTION IS WRONG — this is pre-existing, not caused by acdf4316 (PR #956). `git log -L 40,50:backend/modal_app.py` shows api_image was created without texlive in f2b6ee09 ("feat(modal): create Modal App definition..."), i.e. these three routes have been broken on Modal since the Modal deployment existed. Before acdf4316 the same requests still failed — local_engine_allowed() returned False (Modal cgroup has no docker/kubepods marker, ENVIRONMENT=production), assert_local_engine_allowed raised RuntimeError(ENGINE_UNAVAILABLE_ERROR), and the same broad except turned it into success=false. acdf4316 only changed the failure message ("LaTeX compilation is temporarily unavailable." -> "[Errno 2] ... 'pdflatex'") and was required to unbreak the real latex_image workers. If anything it made the API-container case more diagnosable, not more silent.

3. BLAST RADIUS IS OVERSTATED — two of the three routes have no shipped caller. The web frontend never calls /public/compile or /optimize-and-compile: api-client.ts:1331 compileLatex and :1348 optimizeAndCompile both funnel through submitJob (POST /jobs, job_type latex_compilation/combined), which dispatches to the latex_image/orchestrator containers that do have texlive; anonymous trial compiles go the same way. The public API's POST /api/v1/compile (public_api_routes.py:116) queues a job too. The only live consumer of the broken path is the TUI's `/compile <file>` (packages/tui/src/tools/compile.ts:52), and that path is independently broken regardless of texlive: it types the response as JobSubmitResponse and does wsClient.subscribe(res.job_id) on a synchronous compile that publishes no events, so it would hang even on a box with pdflatex.

Real fix, correctly scoped: these three legacy synchronous routes should either be deleted / made to enqueue a latex job like every other path, or guarded by an explicit engine-presence check (shutil.which("pdflatex")) that returns 503 without charging quota; and routes.py:262 should stop hardcoding latex_available=True on Modal.

confirmed.title: There is no way to run Alembic migrations on Modal — the image explicitly excludes alembic/ and no deploy step applies the schema
confirmed.introducedBy: pre-existing; aggravated by fac3be1b (PR #951), which adds migration 0036_add_auth_rate_limit
confirmed.evidence: `_IGNORE = ["**/.env*", "**/__pycache__/**", "**/*.pyc", "**/alembic/**", "**/test/**", "**/.git/**"]` — the migration tree is not present in any of the three Modal images. `grep -rn "alembic upgrade"` finds it only in Makefile, docker-compose*.yml, k8s/deploy.sh, scripts/deploy/deploy.sh and .github/workflows/ci.yml — every one of those targets a deployment that is not live. main.py's lifespan runs init_db()/redis init/admin reconcile/coupon check, and no migration. (Confirmed nothing at runtime imports alembic: `grep -rn alembic backend/app` → no output, so the exclusion itself is safe.)
confirmed.impact: Schema changes shipped with code are not applied by any deploy. PR #951's `auth_rate_limit` table (used by frontend/src/lib/auth-rate-limit.ts) is a live example: the module fails open, so the shared auth rate limiter is simply off in production until someone runs psql by hand. A future migration that adds a NOT NULL column the ORM writes to would be a hard outage instead.
confirmed.repro: Deploy with `modal deploy modal_app.py`; no step in that command applies migrations, and `alembic/` is not even in the image so it cannot be run with `modal run`.
confirmed.fix: Add a dedicated `@app.function(image=api_image_with_alembic, secrets=_secrets) def migrate(): subprocess.run(["alembic","upgrade","head"], cwd="/backend")`, drop `**/alembic/**` from _IGNORE for that image, and document `modal run modal_app.py::migrate` as a required step before `modal deploy`.
confirmed.correction: Core defect confirmed, wording narrowed: no Modal deploy step applies Alembic migrations, and the migration tree is excluded from all three Modal images, so schema changes shipped with code are never applied automatically to the Modal production database. It is not literally impossible to migrate — the Postgres is an external managed DB, so `DATABASE_URL=<prod> alembic upgrade head` can be run manually from any machine; the gap is the missing automated step (e.g. a `@app.function` migration entrypoint or a documented post-deploy command), not an inability to migrate. Also, 0036_add_auth_rate_limit (fac3be1b / PR #951) is not the first affected migration: 0035_admin_control_plane (commit 154e54c3) is already in the same state, so the drift predates #951 — #951 merely added the first migration whose absence has a user-visible security consequence (auth-rate-limit.ts fails open, disabling the shared auth limiter).

confirmed.title: /jobs/batch refunds the ENTIRE batch cost when the enqueue loop fails partway, giving back optimizations for jobs that already started
confirmed.introducedBy: fac3be1b (#951)
confirmed.evidence:

If the 5th of 10 submits raises, jobs 1-4 are already on the queue and their LLM runs proceed, yet all 10 units are refunded.
confirmed.impact: Free money in the user's favour and a corrupted counter: the user is billed 0 optimizations for N that actually executed on the platform key. The comment above the block asserts the opposite ("a Redis blip or broker error here means the LLM runs never started"), which is only true if the failure happens before the first iteration.

confirmed.correction:
The core defect is real and correctly attributed, but two details in the write-up should be tightened:

1. "Corrupted counter" overstates it. The counter never goes negative or out of sync — all N units were genuinely charged up front by `enforce_quota`, and exactly N are given back. The concrete harm is under-billing: the user is charged 0 for the K jobs (K < N) that were already enqueued and will run on the platform LLM key.

2. Blast radius is bounded. `BatchTailorRequest.jobs` is capped at 10 (11 items -> 422, covered by test_eleven_jobs_returns_422), so a single occurrence leaks at most 9 optimizations, and only on a Redis/broker failure that lands mid-loop. Correct fix: track successfully enqueued jobs inside the loop and refund only `len(body.jobs) - enqueued_count`, or move the try/except inside the loop so each failed submit refunds one unit.

confirmed.title: A failed EXPIRE after a successful INCRBY burns the user's unit AND denies the request, and leaves the counter key with no TTL
confirmed.introducedBy: fac3be1b (#951)
confirmed.evidence:
```
used = int(await redis.incrby(key, cost))
if used == cost:
    await redis.expire(key, _QUOTA_TTL)
except Exception as exc:
    fail_open = limit is None
    ... return QuotaTicket(..., allowed=fail_open, unavailable=True, ...)
```
The INCRBY and the EXPIRE share one try block, so an error on EXPIRE discards a successful increment: the counter keeps the unit, the caller gets `allowed=False, unavailable=True` → 503, and `refund_quota` cannot undo it because it short-circuits: `if ticket.unavailable: return`.
confirmed.impact: On a transient cache-Redis hiccup a free/basic user is charged for a compile that never ran and is told the meter is down. Additionally, when EXPIRE is the call that failed, the key that was just created has no TTL and never expires, so the 40-day self-cleanup the docstring promises silently does not happen for that key.
confirmed.repro: Patch the cache client so `expire` raises while `incrby` succeeds, then call consume_quota: the Redis counter is incremented while the returned ticket has allowed=False, unavailable=True, and refund_quota(ticket) is a no-op.
confirmed.fix: Do the INCRBY and EXPIRE in one Lua script / pipeline (or use `SET key 0 EX ttl NX` followed by INCRBY), and treat an EXPIRE-only failure as non-fatal — the increment already succeeded, so the ticket should reflect the real `used` value rather than reporting the store as unavailable.
confirmed.correction:
The defect is real and correctly attributed to fac3be1b (#951), but severity is better rated low-to-medium rather than medium, and it is two separable issues:

(a) Unit-burn + denial: only occurs when the cache-Redis failure falls in the gap between the successful INCRBY and the EXPIRE on the same connection (connection reset / failover / mid-call timeout). A normal Redis outage fails at INCRBY, where nothing is consumed and fail-closed is the intended behavior. Cost when it does hit: one unit and one 503 for a free/basic user; unlimited plans fail open and are unaffected.

(b) Missing TTL: strictly worse than described in one way — because EXPIRE is only attempted on the creating call (`used == cost`), a single failure means the key never gets a TTL for the rest of its life, so it leaks permanently rather than expiring at 40 days. This is a Redis memory leak only; quota accounting for that period stays correct and the next period uses a fresh key.

Minimal fix: move `expire` out of the shared try (or use `SET key 0 EX ttl NX` + `INCRBY`, or a Lua script / pipeline that does both atomically), and make refund_quota still attempt the DECRBY when the ticket is unavailable-but-incremented (e.g. record on the ticket whether the INCRBY landed).
